content:
Reports indicate that Apple is piloting a new "Live Notes" system at select retail stores. According to the latest reports, the system uses artificial intelligence (AI) to record and transcribe service conversations between Genius Bar staff and customers.

Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman pointed out in his latest issue of the "Power On" newsletter that the Live Notes system allows Apple Store employees to "use AI tools to record the service process, and transcribe and organise conversations with customers into summaries".

The relevant conversation records are subsequently stored in Apple's internal Genius Bar system. Bloomberg stated that the purpose of this move is to allow employees to focus on customer service without being distracted by taking notes.

According to reports, the Live Notes system requires consent from both employees and customers before Genius Bar service begins in order to proceed with recording.

However, Apple retail employees are reportedly concerned about the possible future uses of the Live Notes system:

Currently, the Live Notes system is not mandatory. Bloomberg noted that it remains "unclear" whether Apple will expand the system to more stores, mandate its use, or change the purpose of the conversation records.
